question: Who among the following assumed charge of the Comptroller General of India in November 2024?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **K Sanjay Murthy** assumed charge as the Comptroller General of India in November 2024.
 
• The Comptroller General of India is responsible for overseeing the financial accountability and auditing of government expenditures.
 
• K Sanjay Murthy has a distinguished career in public administration, holding various important positions in the government prior to this appointment.
 
• The role of Comptroller General of India is crucial for ensuring transparency and efficiency in the management of public funds.
 
• K Sanjay Murthy was selected for this position due to his extensive experience in financial management and governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG):**

 
 
• The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is an authority established under Article 148 of the Constitution of India.
 
• The CAG audits all receipts and expenditures of the Government of India and the state governments, including those of bodies and authorities substantially financed by the government.
 
• The CAG's reports are submitted to the President and Governors, who then present them to the respective legislatures.
 
• The position is considered vital for ensuring accountability and transparency in the financial administration of the government.
 
 
 
• **Government Financial Oversight:**
 
 
• Financial oversight ensures that government funds are allocated and spent effectively and in accordance with legal and policy frameworks.
 
• This involves auditing government expenditures, reviewing financial statements, and identifying irregularities or inefficiencies.
 
 
 
• **Public Accountability:**
 
 
• Public accountability is a cornerstone of good governance, requiring transparency in financial and administrative operations.
 
• Institutions like the Comptroller General of India play a critical role in maintaining this accountability.
 
 
 
• **Auditing Standards:**
 
 
• Auditing standards are guidelines for conducting audits to ensure accuracy, reliability, and fairness in financial reporting.
 
• In India, these standards are governed by the CAG and aligned with international best practices.
